text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele presented a plan to squabbling political parties aimed at quelling a crisis which has his government on the ropes. The full details will be made public today.
President Guntis Ulmanis backed Shkele and said that internal political bickering should not be allowed to threaten the reform process.
- The Talsi tragedy claimed the life of another young victim, a seven-year-old boy who died in hospital. The death toll now stands at nine.
- An IMF delegation said that the Latvian government has made great stides on the macroeconomic front.
- Latvia and Ukraine have reached agreement on a free trade pact in agricultural goods.
- The Latvian post office received ten new Mercedes-Benz vans which will replace old Soviet-built trucks.
- The cabinet decided to establish a business administration college in Ventspils, which will open on September 1.
- The total assets of Latvian banks in the first half of 1997 increased by 20.5 percent, reserves rose by 25.9 percent.
